name: Four Seasons Hotel Mumbai
positioning: Glass-tower luxury hotel in Worli with Arabian Sea and skyline views and rooftop bars
best_for: Travelers who value large rooms and sea views

facts.text: Opened May 2008: 207 rooms (182 guest rooms and 25 suites) in a 33-storey building.
Located at 1/136 Dr. E Moses Road, Worli, overlooking the Arabian Sea, the Mahalaxmi Racecourse and the Mumbai skyline.
The design weaves Mumbai's textile heritage into a modern look, with saree-inspired patterns and rich colours.
Dining includes Opus (Western, Asian and Indian, 45 indoor seats) and San:Qi (Japanese, Chinese, Indian and Thai, seating 180).
The spa has 8 treatment rooms on two floors; signature treatments include the White Pearl Facial and Jet Lag Recovery.
The fitness centre is 314 sq m (3,380 sq ft), open 24 hours, with a yoga room and personal trainers on request.
Event space totals 1,667 sq m (17,945 sq ft), including a ballroom with a 750-guest reception capacity.
WhataHotel lists a 5-star rating and a 4.8 average rating for the hotel.

highlights.text: Yacht Club at AER is a 34th-floor rooftop bar with views of the Arabian Sea, known for sunsets and a cocktail menu themed on moods of the sky. It has a retractable roof and stays open all year.
Gimlet Garden at AER is a second rooftop bar, with botanical cocktails built around the bar's own AER Gin and city views.
WhataHotel's pro tip is to book a Harbor View room on floor 25 or above for sunsets over the Arabian Sea.
The spa has heated whirlpools in the men's and women's showers, experience showers and a crystal steam room.

considerations.text: San:Qi, the hotel's Asian restaurant, is listed as currently under renovation on the Four Seasons press fact sheet. Check whether it has reopened before relying on it.
The hotel is in a business district, so reaching traditional tourist attractions takes some travel.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that reflects the five-star positioning.
